metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–7 days, then gradually converges — apply a downward bias correction for the first 7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model tends to overshoot and overcorrect — reduce forecast by 1–2% in the following 3–5 days.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits strong upward bias — apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to the mean forecast.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 38–40), model fails to recognize it — reduce forecast by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overreacts to recent price movements — dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% for 3–5 days after price spikes.
- If true outcome shows downward trend after a spike, model often fails to adjust — apply a 1–3% downward correction for the next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate the “tail” (last 5–7 days) — reduce final 5–7 days by 1–2% to align with observed mean reversion.
